note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Instruction tuning degrades calibration; label smoothing helps but fails for large vocabularies, explained by an entropy bound and fixed by logit scaling and an efficient kernel

nodes.name: SFT degrades calibration
nodes.description: Common supervised fine-tuning (instruction tuning) practices significantly degrade the confidence calibration of open-source LLMs (Fig 1, Fig 2).

nodes.name: Label smoothing regularizes confidence
nodes.description: Label smoothing mixes the target distribution with a uniform distribution using rate beta, acting as a regularizer that makes the model less confident on all samples.

nodes.name: LS preserves calibration in SFT
nodes.description: Across Llama, Gemma and Mistral models fine-tuned on Tulu3 and evaluated on MMLU, label smoothing reduces calibration error with negligible effect on downstream accuracy.

nodes.name: LS gains shrink for large-vocabulary LLMs
nodes.description: The calibration benefit of label smoothing diminishes for smaller Llama3 models (1B, 3B) compared with the 8B model, and is much less visible for large-vocabulary LLMs.

nodes.name: Entropy lower bound tied to hidden and vocab size
nodes.description: A theoretical result links the lower bound of model output entropy to the hidden size D and vocabulary size |V| through the distribution of the final hidden state, limiting the ability to become overconfident.

nodes.name: Temperature and softcapping steer confidence
nodes.description: Temperature scaling (T>1 divides logits) and logit softcapping change the logit scale and hence the entropy bound, allowing models to become overconfident so label smoothing's benefits re-emerge.

nodes.name: Large vocab makes cross-entropy memory heavy
nodes.description: With a large vocabulary, cross-entropy requires materializing an N x |V| logit matrix that dominates the memory footprint of training.

nodes.name: Existing efficient kernels lack LS support
nodes.description: Existing memory-efficient cross-entropy implementations avoid computing the full logit matrix by using only the target row of the classifier head, and so cannot support label smoothing.

nodes.name: Custom LS kernel is memory-efficient
nodes.description: The proposed kernel supports label smoothing with over 75% less peak memory than Liger Kernels, and trails compiled torch by under 10 ms while using about 7% of its memory.

nodes.name: Kernel matches CCE speed
nodes.description: The kernel matches Cut-Cross-Entropy with under 0.5% overhead on the forward pass and under 1% for combined forward/backward.

nodes.name: LS improves ECE/RMS across SFT datasets
nodes.description: With beta=0.1, label smoothing consistently lowers ECE and RMS calibration error on MMLU, HellaSwag and ARC-Easy across Alpaca, Tulu3Mixture and OpenHermes SFT, while preserving accuracy.

isolated_nodes.name: Custom kernel gives same training curves
isolated_nodes.description: Training curves of the custom kernel match torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss with beta=0.1 on LLaMA3.2-3B with Alpaca (Fig 6).

isolated_nodes.name: Best calibration for Llama3-8B and Mistral-7B
isolated_nodes.description: LLaMA3-8B and Mistral-7B achieve the best calibration results, particularly when trained on OpenHermes and Tulu3Mixture (Sec 5.3).

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from SFT miscalibration through label smoothing, its failure on large vocabularies explained by an entropy bound, to logit scaling and an efficient kernel.
